about: Ratchet vectors for the forward-secrecy ratchet (companion change A9 for the iOS port): the primitive known answers walked through one first exchange, the signed ratchet profiles, whole DM transcripts (dm) and single-frame refusals (negative) through the session layer. RatchetVectorTest rebuilds and checks them. See vectors/README.md.

deriveEpoch.note: alice's first epoch, on bob's prekey
bob's first epoch, on alice's epoch-1 key

messageNonce.note: alice's first frame (se 1, n 0, with init): boundAad = aad || headerBindingBytes(header)

spkSigningBytes.sigNote: Ed25519 by the owner's signing key; Tink's is RFC 8032 deterministic, but verify, never compare
Ed25519 by the owner's signing key; Tink's is RFC 8032 deterministic, but verify, never compare

rootTag.note: local storage only, never on the wire: the first 8 HKDF bytes, read big-endian as a signed Int64

export.note: API-only today (the spool's pairwiseRoot and a reserved sealv 2); a port may skip these

profiles.note: deliver 'sequence' in order to one fresh receiver; after each step its pin for that sender is 'expect' (prekey null = no pin). InboundPipelineTest replays it through the real pipeline.

transcriptFormat.note: dm and negative are lists of self-contained transcripts. parties: each party's identity (in identities), the signed prekeys it holds privately (profiles.prekeys names) and pins (the peer prekey it seals against). draws: every injected random value per party, in the order its engine consumes them — keyPair = X25519 priv fixtureBytes(32, seed), iv = the v2 AES-GCM IV fixtureBytes(12, seed); v3 draws no IV. steps run in order; each seal lists the draws it used (drawsUsed). A frame is a chat RelayEnvelope (recipientId = the peer) whose ChatContent.enc is encEnvelope, signed by the sender into wire. aad = aadText's bytes (MessageCrypto.header: id|sender|sentAt|recipient); v3 appends headerBindingBytes(header) and derives its nonce (kats). plaintext is MessageContent.encode() for v2 and MessageContentV2 for v3. An open uses the receiver's own now; expect is RatchetEngine.OpenOutcome's name (OPENED on success) when layer is engine, REFUSED when InboundPipeline refuses it before or around the engine; drop is the DropReason the pipeline records, and resetTriggering whether it feeds the reset heuristic; dropNormative (true everywhere but where a case says otherwise, with a dropNote) says whether a port must record that exact drop or only refuse the frame the same way. An open models the session layer only — RatchetSessions.peekOpen then commitOpen — and nothing a production receiver does around it: IntroSync's init answer, which a responder sends on first contact, is not listed. state is the actor's ratchet state for that peer after the step: secrets as sha256 hex, rootTag as the 16-hex local storage tag, skipped keys as contiguous index runs. Every step is rebuilt and checked by RatchetVectorTest; pipelineReplay cases are replayed through InboundPipeline by InboundPipelineTest, whose ratchet clock is the wall clock, so only a case whose outcome does not depend on now may set pipelineReplay.
ops: seal: actor seals contentBody to peer at now (= sentAt), against pins[peer]
open: actor opens the frame in wire (signed by peer); expect is the outcome
advance: actor seals count v3 frames of any content to peer and discards them
moreOps: reset: actor asks RatchetSessions.sealResetDm(cause) toward peer at now; result is REROOT, MARK or DECLINED (with reason), and decidedBy names the field and floor that decided the plan; a sealed reset is a signed v2 chat frame whose plaintext is MessageContent(ctl = 1)

skip: the frame reaches actor's InboundPipeline after a message row with its id exists; the exists-gate never decrypts it, so no receive key is spent and the receive state does not move, and acknowledges it (acksBack: for a DM to us, a sealed CTL_RECEIPT — the actor's own outbound seal, not listed)
transcriptFormat.floorsBefore: on stage 3b steps: the in-memory floors the actor's RatchetSessions holds for its peer as the step begins (null = no entry; a restart forgets all four): lastReplacementAt (the last replacement or race adoption taken from the peer; an init flagged FLAG_RESET is adopted only RESET_REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS after it, an unflagged one REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS), confirmedAt (when our own init was answered; sealResetDm(UNREADABLE) declines inside RESET_REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS of it), lastResetSentAtInMemory (the no-session fallback only the reset heuristic reads, as the max with the persisted stamp — sealResetDm's plan never reads it: its decline keys on the persisted state.session.lastResetSentAt, which survives a restart) and undecryptableIds (the reset heuristic's distinct-id count).
transcriptFormat.applies: on an open: what InboundPipeline does with what opened — the message row (message), the receipts it records (receipts: acked id and acker), the reaction (LWW at the frame's sentAt), the sealed profile written to the sender's row, and whether it acks the frame back with a sealed CTL_RECEIPT (acksBack). Exactly these and nothing else: InboundPipelineTest checks the deltas.
transcriptFormat.signed: false on a frame in the unsigned point-to-point form (relay = false, sig empty; ADR 059); absent means signed
transcriptFormat.routerDedup: pipeline steps (layer pipeline, skip, applies) model InboundPipeline below MeshRouter's id dedup: a copy of an id the node took inside SeenSet.DEFAULT_TTL_MS is absorbed as deduped before them, unless a reset-triggering open failure reopened the id. So a same-id second copy in a 3b scenario arrives past that window. Engine-layer opens model RatchetSessions alone, router and exists-gate aside (stage 3a's DUPLICATE re-opens included). Neither layer lists the receiver's own ack-backs.

fields.opens: on an open or skip: the index of the step that sealed the frame (a mutation's or twin's source)
fields.content: on a seal of machinery: the MessageContent fields beyond the body — ctl, ack, acks, rp {messageId, emoji (null = retraction)}, pr {name, status, avatarHash, version, openToChat, loraNode, loraKey} — as sealed in plaintext
fields.resealOf: on a seal: the step whose frame it re-seals (same frame id and sentAt, so the same AAD, new bytes)
fields.cleartextAttachmentHash: on a seal: ChatContent.attachmentHash, the cleartext avatar hint MeshManager.sendCtlDm sets
fields.SKIPPED_EXISTS: a skip step's expect: the exists-gate took the frame, see moreOps
fields.pipelineReplay: on a scenario or negative case: InboundPipelineTest replays it through the real pipeline as Bob
fields.fixtures: on a pipelineReplay scenario: rows the receiver holds before it starts (bobSent: Bob's own DMs to Alice)

group.note: group is a list of transcripts in dm's shape over one group (groupId, founders, holdsAtStart). Group frames are chat RelayEnvelopes with group = the sender's roster and no recipientId, ChatContent.enc a v2 group-form EncEnvelope {nonce = the drawn IV, ct, keys = [], g}; aad = id|sender|sentAt|groupId; plaintext is MessageContent.encode(). Seed, ack and request DMs are v2 ctl DMs (MessageContent with ctl 2, 4, 3 and gk), sealed by the sender's RatchetSessions like any DM. A seed DM's own seal step comes after the groupSeal that minted it, its outbox stamp already in its groupState.
ops: groupSeal: actor seals contentBody to the group through GroupRatchetSessions.sealGroup; minted is the seed a mint drew (else null); the seed DMs a mint sends follow as seal steps

groupOpen: actor opens a group frame through GroupRatchetSessions (peek, commit); expect is GroupRatchetEngine.OpenOutcome's name, keyRequestDue whether a NO_KEY or AEAD_FAIL fired the key-request heuristic
depart: GroupRepository.recordDeparture on actor: roster shrinks, send chain retired, the leaver's outbox row dropped
restore: a backup restore onto actor: every ratchet table empty, group rows and identity kept

fields.groupState: on every group-section step: the actor's roster (names), shared root, send chains (retired = key-less), receive chains, skipped keys and seed outbox
fields.groupHeader: a group frame's GroupRatchetHeader {se, n}; its AAD's thread is the group id
fields.groupSeed: a draw kind: a group epoch seed, fixtureBytes(32, seed)
fields.applies.groupPinned: the roster the receiver pinned from the seed (InboundPipeline.pinRosterFromSeed) when it held no row
fields.applies.seeds: per seed carried: ADOPT, ALREADY_KNOWN or STALE (GroupRatchetEngine.adoptSeed's verdict)
fields.applies.groupKeyAckBack: the epoch the receiver acks back in a CTL_GROUP_KEY_ACK, or null
fields.applies.custodyReplay: whether the receiver replays its own custody's frames from that sender after the adoption
fields.applies.groupRoot: the root a CTL_GROUP_KEY offered and whether the receiver adopted it (GroupRootPolicy.adoptable)
fields.applies.groupKeyAcked: the epoch an inbound ack stamped in the outbox
fields.applies.resetAnswer: a CTL_SESSION_RESET's post-commit answer: re-seal unacked DMs, force-flush seeds
fields.pipelineReceivers: the parties InboundPipelineTest replays the scenario as, each through its own pipeline; replaysOwnSeals: it also re-seals that party's own DM seal steps through RatchetSessions.sealDm from the step's draws and asserts the bytes
fields.pipelineChecked: on every group-section step: true when InboundPipelineTest checks it (an open's applies and drop, or an own seal's bytes); false when only the transcript's mirror of MeshManager/InboundPipeline states it
fields.keyRequestDue: checked against the mirror only: InboundPipeline.decryptAndDeliverGroup takes the 48 h age gate's now from System.currentTimeMillis(), so a replay of these dated frames never reaches the heuristic
fields.applies.rootGossip: MeshManager.onGroupRootCtl's post-commit answer: onward (members sent the adopted root) and floored (members skipped by seedSendFloorOpen), or back (whether ours went back to the sender) with why not; the sends are listed as the receiver's own seal steps
fields.fixtures.roots: a shared root a party holds at the start: a stated fixtureBytes(32, seed), not a draw
fields.pipelineClock: a pipeline-replayed open (this section's and dm's pipelineReplay ones) runs at the wall clock, not the step's now: InboundPipeline.decryptAndDeliverV2 and decryptAndDeliverGroup read System.currentTimeMillis(); only seals, re-seals and the pipeline's clock() paths take the step's now

carol.note: carol is a list of transcripts in dm's shape, each a DM session between Carol (the iPhone, the carol identity, prekey carolSpk1) and one Android party. Every draw is listed per party, Carol's included: inject Carol's in order and her seal steps (header, nonce, ct, encEnvelope, wire) must come out byte for byte. The frame after each plain DM open is the receiver's delivery tick. Every opener here is v3, the form Android sends to a CAP_CRYPTO_V3 peer (the init bound into the AAD); dm's committed firstContact opener is the v2 inbound form, still accepted. InboundPipelineTest compares the Android receiver's session after each checked open (after the tick, for one that ticks back) with the step's state, except recvEpochs' lastUsedAt and the session's prevRootExpiresAt: the pipeline's opens stamp those from System.currentTimeMillis(), not the step's now.

fields.sealedByPipeline: true on a seal step the sealing party's own InboundPipeline makes in answer to the open just before it (sealDmReceipt's CTL_RECEIPT tick, v3 here), not one its user sends; that open's applies.tickStep names it. A replay checks it through the open (its draws, and a receipt acking the frame), never as a seal of its own: the pipeline mints the tick's frame id and clock, so its ct differs from the listed one while the chain state it leaves is the same
fields.applies.tickStep: on an open that ticks back: the index of the sealedByPipeline step that is the tick

dm.name: firstContact
dm.note: Alice initiates to Bob's signed prekey (X3DH) and opens send epoch 1 on it (pe 0): a v2 frame, then a v3 one, both carrying the init because the session is unconfirmed. Bob, holding nothing, responds from the first frame's init and opens both; a responder's session is confirmed from the start.

dm.name: confirm
dm.note: firstContact, then Bob's first frame: his epoch 1, DHed on Alice's epoch-1 key (pe 1). Opening it confirms Alice's session (the peer sealed against an epoch of hers), so her next frame drops the init — and, her peer's base having moved past her epoch's, opens her epoch 2 on Bob's epoch 1.

dm.name: turnaround
dm.note: confirm, then the healing rule both ways: a second Alice frame stays in her epoch 2 (Bob has not moved), Bob's answer opens his epoch 2 on her epoch 2 — sealed v2, so it draws an IV — and Alice's answer to that opens her epoch 3. Every conversational turnaround is a fresh DH.

dm.name: epochCap
dm.note: MAX_EPOCH_MESSAGES = 200. firstContact leaves Alice's epoch 1 at n 2; an advance step seals n 2..197 unlisted (v3, no draws), and only the boundary frames are listed: n 198, n 199, and the next seal, which the full epoch moves to epoch 2 (still pe 0 on Bob's prekey, still with the init). Bob opens n 198 first, so n 2..197 become skipped keys, then n 199 and epoch 2's n 0.

steps.note: seal 196 v3 frames of any content and discard them: they advance the send chain from n 2 and move nothing else

dm.name: epochAge
dm.note: MAX_EPOCH_AGE_MS = 24 h, against the epoch's sendEpochStartedAt (Alice's first seal): a seal 1 ms short of it stays in epoch 1, a seal at it opens epoch 2.

dm.name: outOfOrder
dm.note: Alice seals n 0 (v2) to n 3; Bob's first frame is n 3, which establishes his session from its init and stores n 0..2 as skipped keys. n 1 and n 2 open on theirs, then n 0 (v2), and re-opening n 1 or n 3 finds the index consumed: DUPLICATE, which never triggers a reset.

dm.name: ctlPlane
dm.note: Alice's machinery to Bob, all before she ever opens a frame of his (so every frame still carries her init, and a pipeline replay as Bob reaches each one): a sealed CTL_RECEIPT with one ack and one with an acks batch (docs/ENCRYPTED_RECEIPTS_REACTIONS.md, ADR 018), a CTL_REACTION and its retraction, a sealed CTL_PROFILE (docs/SEALED_PROFILE_UPDATES.md), a plain DM carrying inline acks (CAP_INLINE_ACK, ADR 054), the unsigned v3 live-link tick (ADR 059, accepted) and an unsigned plain DM (refused by the pipeline before commit, UNSIGNED_REFUSED) whose signed twin then opens. The ids Alice acks and reacts to are Bob's own DMs to her (fixtures.bobSent); `applies` on each open is what InboundPipeline does with it, and InboundPipelineTest replays the scenario to check it. Bob's own receipts for her plain DMs are his outbound frames, sealed from his own randomness, and are not listed.

steps.note: the receiver applies the inline acks as receipts in the same commit as the row, then acks the DM itself
the unsigned live-link tick: relay = false, an empty sig
a plain DM in the unsigned form (a stripped signature)

the signed twin opens on the unspent index. It arrives past SeenSet.DEFAULT_TTL_MS after the refused copy: the router marked the id seen before the pipeline refused it (an UNSIGNED_REFUSED does not reopen it), so a twin inside that window is absorbed as deduped and never reaches the pipeline

dm.name: raceWinnerArrivesFirst
dm.note: A both-initiate race, the winner's init first (ADR 2026-09.pz9g, FSR §7): the init whose initiator has the smaller node id wins, never the earlier stamp. Alice's id sorts first. Bob, holding his own unconfirmed init, opens hers and adopts her root (his own drains as prevRoot, his receive state is purged, and the adoption starts his replacement floor: lastReplacementAt). Alice then opens Bob's opening DM under his root as a read-only candidate: it opens, and her session stays unconfirmed on her own root.

steps.note: the loser adopts the winner's root
the winner reads the loser's DM under the loser's root, read-only
the loser's answer under the winner's root confirms the winner

dm.name: raceLoserArrivesFirst
dm.note: The same race, the loser's init first (ADR 2026-09.pz9g): Alice keeps her root and reads Bob's opening DM read-only (it records his init's ephemeral, so a re-serve is inert), then Bob adopts her root on her frame. The frames are raceWinnerArrivesFirst's, byte for byte; only the arrival order differs, and both orders end on Alice's root.

steps.note: the winner keeps its root and reads the loser's DM read-only
the loser adopts the winner's root
the loser's answer under the winner's root confirms the winner

dm.name: lateLoserOpening
dm.note: #83: Bob lost the race and answered under Alice's root before his own opening DM reached her, so Alice confirmed without ever resolving his init. His DM arrives late: the remnant guard refuses to adopt its init (a confirmed initiator with no peer init resolved, the init from the side that loses the tiebreak, no FLAG_RESET), and the loser's root is offered as a trailing read-only candidate. The DM opens and records nothing — not even the init's ephemeral — and its re-serve is DUPLICATE on the row it stored.

steps.note: the loser adopts the winner's root
the loser's answer under the winner's root confirms the winner
the late loser's opening DM, read under its own root and never anchored

a re-serve past SeenSet.DEFAULT_TTL_MS (inside it the router absorbs the id). Session layer only: on a whole node the row the first open wrote makes the exists-gate skip this copy; DUPLICATE is what RatchetSessions answers for a re-serve with no row (remnantCandidates' KDoc)

dm.name: reRootReset
dm.note: After confirm, Alice seals three more old-era frames (her epoch 2, n 1..3) that are slow to arrive, then asks for a reset (ON_DEMAND): a fresh X3DH init flagged FLAG_RESET, her numbering restarted at epoch 1, her own receive state purged, the old root kept as prevRoot (ADR 023, ADR 027). The reset seals v2 though the pair reads v3 — resets stay v2 (ADR 059, FSR §5). Bob adopts it (his replacement floor starts; his old root drains as prevRoot until prevRootExpiresAt = his open + PREV_ROOT_TTL_MS). n 1 drains on the old root and stores its chain under the old root's tag; the new era's epoch 2 then opens on a fresh chain beside it, though the number is the same (#135, ADR 2026-10.gcrd). n 2 opens 1 ms before Bob's prevRootExpiresAt; n 3 at it no longer does (AEAD_FAIL).

steps.decidedBy: state.session: confirmed, so no pending init; cause ON_DEMAND, so the answered-init floor does not apply

steps.note: FLAG_RESET init adopted: no replacement from Alice in the last minute

an old-era frame drains under prevRoot. Re-deriving Alice's old epoch 2 after the purge banks a skipped key for idx 0, which Bob already consumed before the reset, so a row-less re-serve of that frame would open once more inside the drain window: the cost ADR 2026-10.gcrd accepts, not a bug
Bob answered under the new root: Alice confirms
#135: epoch 2 again, under the new root, beside the old root's epoch-2 row
1 ms inside the drain window
at prevRootExpiresAt the old root is no longer a candidate

dm.name: confirmEra
dm.note: #87 (ADR 2026-09.pz9g): after confirm, Bob seals a frame on his epoch 2 (against Alice's old epoch 2) and Alice resets before it arrives. It opens under her prevRoot — her old epoch 2's key survives the reset, which re-minted only epoch 1 — but a frame drained under any root but the active one moves no era, so her replacement session stays unconfirmed and her next frame still carries the reset's init (flags 0 on a follow-up: only the reset frame itself is flagged). Bob adopts the reset, reads the follow-up on the same init, and his first new-era frame confirms her.

steps.decidedBy: state.session: confirmed, so no pending init; cause ON_DEMAND, so the answered-init floor does not apply

steps.note: #87: opens under prevRoot and leaves the new session unconfirmed
the same init again: resolved idempotently by its ephemeral
a fresh epoch under the active root: confirms

dm.name: resetPlans
dm.note: RatchetSessions.sealResetDm never seals a reset the peer would refuse (ADR 2026-09.qerd, #85/#86). Against Alice's own pending plain init it seals the Mark: the reset marker under the init she already has out, its header flagged FLAG_RESET, no new root, stamping lastResetSentAt. A second ask inside RESET_REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS (1 min) of that stamp is declined. Once Bob's answer confirms her init (confirmedAt), an UNREADABLE ask inside that minute is declined; at a minute it re-roots, and Bob — with no replacement from her before — adopts it.

steps.decidedBy: state.session: our own init pending (weAreInitiator, !confirmed, initPkid = the pinned prekey) and plain (lastResetSentAt < establishedAt)
steps.note: our own init is pending and plain (session.lastResetSentAt 0 < establishedAt): the Mark

steps.reason: our reset is still on its way
steps.decidedBy: state.session.lastResetSentAt (persisted): now - it < RESET_REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS on a pending init
steps.note: 10 s after the Mark: inside the 1 min floor
the Mark's init is the one Bob holds: idempotent, no purge
Bob answered our init: confirmedAt is stamped

steps.reason: the peer adopted our init under a minute ago
steps.decidedBy: floorsBefore.confirmedAt (cause UNREADABLE, our own init answered): declined while now - it < RESET_REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS
steps.note: 30 s after confirmedAt

steps.decidedBy: floorsBefore.confirmedAt (cause UNREADABLE, our own init answered): declined while now - it < RESET_REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS
steps.note: exactly 1 min after confirmedAt: outside the floor
adopted: Bob has no replacement from Alice to floor it

dm.name: resealNewFirst
dm.note: The re-seal pair (MeshManager.resealAndFlood, ADR 2026-09.qerd): a DM Alice sealed in the old era is still unread when Bob resets, so on his reset marker she re-seals it — same frame id, same sentAt, new bytes under the new session. The re-sealed copy reaches Bob first and opens; the original arrives later, and the exists-gate (a message row with its id) acknowledges it without decrypting. Decrypted, it would fail: Bob's reset purged his receive state and re-minted his epoch 1, which it was sealed against.

steps.decidedBy: state.session: Bob responded (weAreInitiator false), so no pending init and no answered-init floor

steps.note: Alice adopts Bob's reset; its marker makes her re-seal what he has not acked
the same row re-sealed: its id and sentAt (so the same AAD) under the new session, new bytes

the original, after the copy's row exists: acknowledged, never decrypted. It arrives past SeenSet.DEFAULT_TTL_MS after the copy, because inside that window the router absorbs the same id as deduped before the pipeline sees it (a custody re-serve after the window is what reaches the gate)

dm.name: resealOldFirst
dm.note: The re-seal pair the other way round (ADR 2026-09.qerd): Bob opened the original before he reset, but his receipt had not reached Alice, so she re-seals it anyway. The copy lands on the row the original wrote, and the exists-gate acknowledges it without decrypting: no chain key is spent on it.

steps.decidedBy: state.session: Bob responded (weAreInitiator false), so no pending init and no answered-init floor

steps.note: Alice adopts Bob's reset; its marker makes her re-seal what he has not acked
the same row re-sealed: its id and sentAt (so the same AAD) under the new session, new bytes

the re-sealed copy, after the original's row exists: acknowledged, never decrypted. It arrives past SeenSet.DEFAULT_TTL_MS after the original, because inside that window the router absorbs the same id as deduped before the pipeline sees it (the original opened, so nothing reopens the id)

negative.name: seAtCeiling
negative.note: se = MAX_EPOCH_NUMBER is in bounds: the frame reaches the key work, derives a key Alice never sealed under, and fails its AEAD — reset-triggering, unlike every out-of-bounds case

negative.name: peZeroWithoutInit
negative.note: pe 0 names our signed prekey, legal only with an init

negative.name: ekLowOrder
negative.note: an ek of small order: X25519 refuses it, and the engine reports BAD_HEADER (never a missing key)

negative.name: prekeyGone
negative.note: the init names a prekey Bob no longer holds (pruned): EPOCH_GONE, reset-triggering

negative.name: noInitNoSession
negative.note: a frame with no init (pe 1, so in bounds) to a Bob holding no session: NO_SESSION, reset-triggering

negative.name: ownEpochGone
negative.note: Bob holds the session (he opened the first frame), and a frame opens a new epoch (se 2) on an epoch of his he never minted (pe 5): EPOCH_GONE before any AEAD

negative.name: ctTampered
negative.note: the v3 frame with its last ciphertext byte flipped: every key resolves and the AEAD refuses. Nothing commits — Bob still holds no session

negative.name: initEphLowOrder
negative.note: an init whose eph is of small order. The engine does not type this: X25519 throws inside the X3DH respond, out of RatchetEngine.open, and InboundPipeline's runCatching drops it as DECRYPT_FAILED — before onRatchetFailure, so it never reaches the reset heuristic, and nothing commits

steps.dropNote: not normative: a port must refuse this frame with nothing committed and without feeding the reset heuristic, but may name the drop BAD_HEADER or DECRYPT_FAILED (Kotlin's engine throws here and the pipeline's catch records DECRYPT_FAILED)

negative.name: v3NonEmptyNonce
negative.note: a v3 envelope carries its nonce field empty (it is derived); a 12-byte one is malformed. Refused by InboundPipeline.nonceShapeValid before the engine

negative.name: v2EmptyNonce
negative.note: the mirror: a v2 envelope carries a 12-byte IV, so an empty one is malformed (nonceShapeValid)

negative.name: v3ToGroup
negative.note: v3 is the DM form by rule: Alice's v3 frame re-addressed to the group of alice, bob and carol (recipientId absent) routes to the DM arm and is refused there, before any group or reset logic. The receiver holds the group (its members are in groupMembers)

group.name: groupSeed
group.note: GFS §3 and ADR 017, with the roster on the seed (work item #47, ADR 2026-09.mjaj): Alice's first group message mints her epoch 1, and MeshManager.distributeGroupSeed seals one CTL_GROUP_KEY DM per other member (v2, the named plaintext, never v3) before the group frame floods. The DM's GroupKeyPayload carries the seed and the founding roster (gk.group), so Bob, holding no row, pins the group from it, adopts the chain and acks the epoch back (CTL_GROUP_KEY_ACK, InboundPipeline.ackGroupSeed); Alice's outbox records each ack (GroupRatchetSessions.onKeyAck). Carol does the same.

the seed distribution of epoch 1
the seed distribution of epoch 1
first contact and the seed: Bob pins the roster from it
the seed's acknowledgement
the ack stamps Alice's outbox: ackedEpoch 1 for bob
the seed's acknowledgement

group.name: groupFrames
group.note: GFS §5: after groupSeed's opening, Alice's next four group frames ride her epoch 1 (no mint, one IV each), and a group-form CTL_REACTION (MeshManager.sealGroupReaction: the same group seal, never persisted as a message, applied atomically with the chain advance). Bob opens n 3 first (n 1 and n 2 banked as skipped keys), then n 1, n 2 and n 4; a re-serve of n 2 past SeenSet.DEFAULT_TTL_MS is DUPLICATE at the group engine (on a whole node the row it wrote makes the exists-gate skip it first).

steps.note: the first send mints epoch 1
the seed distribution of epoch 1
the seed distribution of epoch 1
first contact and the seed: Bob pins the roster from it
n 3 before n 1 and n 2: two skipped keys
engine layer only: the router absorbs it inside the window, and the exists-gate after it

group.name: groupKeyRequest
group.note: GFS §7 and ADR 017: Bob sends to the group and his seed DM to Carol is lost. Each of his frames is NO_KEY at Carol, and the third distinct one fires the key-request heuristic (REQUEST_DISTINCT_FRAMES, under KEY_REQUEST_MIN_INTERVAL_MS and the REQUEST_MAX_FRAME_AGE_MS gate: keyRequestDue). Carol seals a CTL_GROUP_KEY_REQ; Bob's pipeline hands it to MeshManager.redistributeGroupKey, which re-seals his current seeds to her (no new epoch; the per-member SEED_RESEND_FLOOR_MS floor is open, nothing went to her since). Carol adopts, acks, and her custody replay opens the three frames. Carol and Bob already share a DM session (her "Hi Bob"), so no race is in play.

the seed distribution of epoch 1
the seed distribution of epoch 1
the key request, after the heuristic fired
the request goes to MeshManager.redistributeGroupKey after the commit
the key-request answer: current seeds, no new epoch
replayed from Carol's own custody after the adoption

group.name: groupRoot
group.note: docs/SPOOL_PROTOCOL.md §3.2 (MeshManager.gossipGroupRoot / adoptGroupRoot, GroupRootPolicy): Alice holds root v1 and, never having sealed a group frame, gossips it root-only — a CTL_GROUP_KEY with empty keys. Bob pins the roster from it and adopts the root (no seed, so no ack). Carol, partitioned past MINT_GRACE_MS, minted her own v1; the (version, minter) order prefers hers (her node id sorts after Alice's), so Bob adopts it too. Each adoption goes onward (MeshManager.onGroupRootCtl → gossipGroupRoot(skip = sender)): Alice's root to Carol, then Carol's to Alice — Bob's own root-only DMs, listed. Bob adopts the re-mint too, so he holds both eras' chains for the epoch (GFS §4 rule 5: receivers key rows by (group, sender, epoch, mintedAt)). Each era's n 3 opens on its own chain and banks n 0 to 2 as skipped keys under its own mint: two keys at each index. n 1 opens the new era's first, then the old era's; n 2 the other way round. Every open spends only its own mint's key: before #177 spending one deleted both, and the other era's frame at that index read as DUPLICATE for good, since both chains are past it and a re-sent seed never rewinds a chain. A re-serve of either n 1 past SeenSet.DEFAULT_TTL_MS is then DUPLICATE at the group engine.

carol.name: raceBobCarolWinnerFirst
carol.note: A both-initiate race (ADR 2026-09.pz9g, FSR §7): Carol and Bob each seal an opening DM to the other's prekey before hearing from the other. The init whose initiator has the smaller node id wins, never the earlier stamp (RatchetEngine.resolveRace): the loser adopts the winner's root (its own drains as prevRoot, its receive state is purged, the adoption starts its replacement floor); the winner reads the loser's DM under the loser's root and keeps its root, anchors the loser's init by its ephemeral, and drains the loser's root as prevRoot, without taking its epoch as a DH base. Both openers are v3, as CryptoScheme picks between these peers (FSR §5, ADR 059): the init is bound into the AAD, and each root candidate derives its own nonce. The winner's DM reaches the loser first: the loser adopts on it and its tick back is its first frame under the winning root; the winner then reads the loser's DM and ticks it from its own still unconfirmed session; the loser's tick confirms the winner. Carol (the iPhone) wins: her node id sorts before Bob's. The winner is the receiver here only in Carol's steps, so the Android replay is Bob, the loser.
